bdf.distributions.GammaMSLambdaNegBin

class bdf.distributions.GammaMSLambdaNegBin(params)[source]

Bases: BDFDistribution[GammaMSLambdaNegBinParams]

Negative Binomial with Gamma prior on mean λ (Mean-Strength parameterization).

Usage: dist="GammaMSLambdaNegBin"

Model Specification:

  • Prior: \(\lambda \sim \text{Gamma}(\alpha_0, \beta_0)\) where \(\alpha_0 = m \cdot \lambda_0\), \(\beta_0 = m\)

  • Likelihood: \(y \mid \lambda, \phi \sim \text{NegBin}(\lambda, \phi)\)

  • Posterior: \(\lambda \mid y \sim \text{Gamma}(\alpha_0 + \sum y_i, \beta_0 + n)\)

Key Properties:

  • Exact Linear Shrinkage: \(E[\lambda \mid y] = \frac{m \lambda_0 + n \bar{y}}{m + n}\)

  • Closed-form Evidence: Supports NLE scoring via Bayesian marginal likelihood

  • Posterior Predictive: Integrates out \(\lambda\) uncertainty for robust predictions

Parameters:

  • mean_lambda (float, default=1.0) – Prior mean for \(\lambda\) (\(\lambda_0\)). Grand mean, shrinkage target.

  • strength_lambda (float, default=1.0) – Prior strength (pseudo-observations, \(m\)). Higher = stronger regularization.

  • phi (float or None, default=None) – Dispersion parameter \(\phi\). If None, estimated via MoM per leaf. If provided, treated as fixed hyperparameter across all leaves.

  • score_method ({'nle', 'nll'}, default='nle') – Scoring method. ‘nle’ uses exact Bayesian evidence.

  • use_posterior_predictive (bool, default=True) – If True, uses posterior predictive (marginalizes \(\lambda\) uncertainty).

Examples

>>> from bdf import BDFRegressor
>>> model = BDFRegressor(
...     dist="GammaMSLambdaNegBin",
...     params={
...         "mean_lambda": "auto",      # Use global mean
...         "strength_lambda": 1.0,     # 1 pseudo-observation
...         "phi": None,                # Estimate per leaf
...         "score_method": "nle",
...         "use_posterior_predictive": True,
...     }
... )
>>> model.fit(X, y)

Notes

This is a fully conjugate Bayesian model. The Gamma prior on \(\lambda\) combined with the Negative Binomial likelihood gives:

  • Exact conjugate updates (no approximations)

  • Interpretable hyperparameters: strength_lambda = number of pseudo-observations

  • Linear shrinkage: \(E[\lambda \mid y] = \frac{m \lambda_0 + n \bar{y}}{m + n}\)

The dispersion parameter \(\phi\) (also called \(r\)) is estimated via Method of Moments when not provided, allowing adaptive overdispersion per leaf.
